<!-- pr-reviewer: 45dbc71c9f3452d289c383ed01927c6dc367b7c2 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

## What looks good
- Domain code sits in `camcraft-sim` (`crates/sim/src/chuck.rs`); `app` only wires the accessory kinds, defaults, the `OnStock` placement and MCP. No new crate dependency, no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside tests, no snapshot PNG touched, `Refs #1442` (not a closing keyword), follow-up #1468 named, decision file present.
- Envelope read from the figures (safety floor):
  - Round outer faces are drawn with flats on the true circle (`flats_on` = r / cos(pi/64), +0.12%), so the body and nose enclose the real circle. Nothing outside comes out smaller than typed.
  - Body length, jaw height, jaw reach (grip radius + jaw length) and nose length are exact box/ring bounds.
  - Jaws are 3 at 120 deg and 4 at 90 deg, the first on +x. The z = 0 face frame is stated, and the fit puts the origin on the stock axis at the stock underside (a collet one nose length higher).
  - A jaw box's corners reach slightly past its nominal reach, which is extra steel, so conservative.
- Validation is at command creation and refused by name: non-finite, zero, negative, > 5000 mm, bore not inside the body, jaws past the body, jaws meeting, collet bore not inside the nose, nose wider than the body, round-stock check (0.5% tolerance), non-chuck kinds, no stock. `fit.check()` re-runs after the grip is set.
- The holder test goes through the real path: holder in the jaws gives a `FixtureHit` and `post_setup` is blocked ("holder at move N strikes a fixture"); the same holder 5 mm higher posts, so the control is meaningful.

## Results merged with main
On the self-hosted runner: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/43473701147 (conclusion success; trial merge with main 7c21c9c clean).
- Quick gate: sim suites ok (18 s), app suites ok (61 s), 0 failed.
- Clippy `-p camcraft-app -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.
- Not run by me: ui lib tests (the PR reports 6 passed for `fixture_accessory`), no `cfg(windows)` lines in the diff.

## Requested before merge
None.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. `crates/sim/src/chuck.rs`, `ring()` and the module header ("Bores are drawn the same way... slightly less air - safe side", also in the decision file): the inner bore also goes through `flats_on`, which makes the drawn hole slightly LARGER than the real bore (vertices outside the circle). Bore-wall steel is therefore up to 0.12% of the bore radius short (0.012 mm on a 20 mm collet bore). Harmless in practice, but the comment states the opposite; either fix the wording or draw the inner circle with vertices on it.
2. The envelope tests probe points 0.5-1 mm from the rim and tip, so a shrink of under 0.5 mm in the body or jaw reach would not fail the sim test. The app test pins the drawn radius to 40..40.1 and z bounds exactly, and jaw height and body length are pinned exactly. Tighter probes (for example 79.95 and 80.05) would close that.
3. Fit uses `max(dx, dy)` for the diameter with a 0.5% roundness tolerance, so on a slightly oval stock the jaws sit up to 0.25% of the diameter off the stock. Within the stated tolerance.
4. Project file: three new `Accessory` variants. An older build opening a project that holds a chuck would not know the kinds. Please state whether this needs a format-version note (no forward migration is needed, as nothing existing changes).
5. Screenshots of the chucks in the viewport and the dialog are owed by the maintainer (the PR says so).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
